about: Q4 parity harness scenarios and tolerances (tools/parity/README.md). A tolerance key is a metric family prefix, optionally with a [Faction] bracket, or an exact metric id; the most specific key wins. abs / rel widen the retail envelope [min, max] of the reference runs; min_overlap grades a type mix; info = reported, not graded. Every entry says why.

hotm_galactic.title: Galactic Conquest, Heart of the Maw (Sandbox_Heart_Of_The_Maw_Empire), idle human Empire, Rebel and Underworld AI, seed 0, 13501 ticks (10 fiscal cycles)

references.note: reader 1: no credits, no production queues (travel, fleets and outcomes only); 577 missed ticks

excluded_references.20261103-152619-galactic-vanilla-lua: q2f t08 (2026-11-08): its Lua plan hooks killed retail's own plan threads (records table lost to PGBase Flush_G, docs/re/LUA_SCRIPT_OUTPUT.md section 4), so its AI production and fleet moves are not retail behaviour (Rebel fleet departures 19 vs 71). Replace it with a run of the fixed kit

hotm_galactic.kit: tools/probe_mod/q2_traces/run_lua_probe.cmd (or run_galactic.cmd; -NonInteractive drives the menus), README in that folder

geonosis_skirmish.title: Space skirmish, (2) Battle Over Geonosis (_MP_SPACE_GEONOSIS), idle human Empire vs Rebel AI (Medium), 6000 credits, 5400 ticks

references.note: seeded 0x41ccdfe4 (the port host uses its own seed); every tick sampled

geonosis_skirmish.kit: tools/probe_mod/q2_traces/run_skirmish.cmd -LuaProbe (-NonInteractive drives the menus), README in that folder

travel.hop_ticks.why: keyed by faction and route; a hop takes its fleet's speed (the units' Hyperspace_Speed, the Underworld corruption bonus), so one route has several durations in retail (Underworld Nal Hutta -> Shola: 89 and 107 ticks) and each port hop must lie within tolerance of some retail hop of that route. A leg is timed from the last sample at its start planet to the first sample at its end planet, a trip passing a planet centre is split there (same rule on both sides, q4hf t04); retail hops of one route and fleet differ by up to 6 ticks (Rebel Kamino -> Shola 221 / 227, Mon Calamari -> Shola 74 / 80), so 3%, at least 3 ticks; a wrong speed multiplier shows as 100+ ticks (tools/probe_mod/g1_hops/README.md)

build.ticks.why: the shortest completed build per type and planet: retail from its queue start to leaving the queue (production.q2q: items finish 2 ticks after start + frames), the port from the AI build order to the new object in its state trace. The retail runs themselves differ by 5% on one planet (mining facility at Mon Calamari 686 vs 722 ticks, Y-wings 344 vs 362: a build-time modifier present in one run only), so 5%, at least 3 ticks

econ.cycle_tick.why: the fiscal period is data (45 s = 1350 frames) and the first payment rule is known (q2f t02): exact; a retail cycle seen across missed samples is a window and the port tick must fall inside it

econ.income_cycle1.why: the first payment comes before AI ownership or structure choices can differ much: planet incomes, starting structures and corruption are data; 1% covers f32 credit arithmetic

econ.income_mean.why: later payments follow the planets and mining facilities owned, which follow AI choices; the retail runs already differ in these, 10% on top of their envelope

econ.credits_at.why: an AI balance is income minus spending, and AI spending timing differs between runs (the HotM retail runs end with 22 and 899 Rebel credits); 25% on top of the retail envelope. The income metrics are the economy check, this one catches gross spending differences

econ.credits_at[Empire].why: the Empire is the idle human in both scenarios: it never spends, so its balance is income alone and must match closely

ai.build_count.why: how many items an AI queues depends on its budget and the RNG draw order, which the port does not reproduce draw for draw; 25% (at least 2 items) on top of the retail envelope

ai.build_mix.why: an AI must build the same kind of units and structures: its items (multiset of types) must overlap the closest retail run at least as much as the retail runs overlap each other, capped at 0.5 (HotM retail runs overlap only 0.30 for the Rebel and 0.43 for the Underworld; a single reference run uses 0.5)

ai.fleet_departures.why: fleet moves follow AI plans and the RNG; the retail runs of one scenario already differ widely (their envelope); 25% (at least 2) on top

ai.fleet_targets.why: the AI must send fleets to the same planets: its departures by target planet must overlap the closest retail run at least as much as the retail runs overlap each other, capped at 0.5 (HotM retail: Rebel 0.23-0.80, Underworld 0.64-0.80)

ai.first_build_tick.why: the first AI decisions come before any run-to-run difference builds up: within 1 s (30 ticks) of retail

ai.first_departure_tick.why: as ai.first_build_tick: the first fleet order within 1 s of retail

ai.first_build_frame.why: skirmish units are counted from snapshots every 600 frames (the port host's state cadence): one snapshot of slack

outcome.planets_final.why: a planet is one discrete outcome; the retail runs already span the outcomes seen (Shola captured or not)

outcome.captures.why: planet captures per faction: one capture more or less than the retail envelope

outcome.owner_changes.why: total planet owner changes: one more or less than the retail envelope

outcome.units_final.why: units alive at the end of a skirmish: production and losses both depend on AI timing; 20% (at least 2 units)

outcome.units_lost.why: units destroyed during the skirmish: 25% (at least 2 units)

outcome.battle_ended.why: whether the battle ends before the tick limit is a discrete outcome

combat.damage_taken.why: hull lost per faction over the battle: weapon damage is data, but targeting and fire timing follow AI orders; 25%

combat.first_shot_frame.why: first projectile of the battle: within 10 s (300 frames)

diag.why: synced-RNG draws are an implementation detail; reported to explain divergences, never graded (parity is behaviour)
